**Whole-PR performance: block** at `f5c25d425edead58c176cacebd188ca3ac6fa1b8`. **Workshop P163-F001 is closed on cost; new P163-F002 concerns the sensor command.**

**P163-F002: put the new heavy Cargo stage through the existing resource-safe build/test path and price the composite gate.** `justfile:236-237` runs raw `cargo test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib route_inventory_tests`. A cold invocation can compile and execute tests in that one inherited-priority command; the recipe does not apply the required background/niced compilation versus nice-only test split, nor the existing shared-build resource controls. `harness checks` delegates to that recipe through `ctx.exec`; marking it heavy only makes --quick skip it. The advertised standalone command can therefore compile foreground on the shared machine.

Use the existing `just shared-build` path (or equivalent existing resource-safe compile/test separation) for this newly added recipe. This finding is on the new stage, not a request to refactor unrelated legacy Rust recipes. Backpressure must also distinguish cold compilation, warm execution, and full-gate repetition; "one enumeration plus one JSON read per harness checks invocation" is not the full-gate total.

**Actual sensor work:** the module has six tests. Only its positive inventory test reads the real JSON and builds/probes the router; the other five use in-memory sets/fixtures. At this head Endpoint::ALL has 59 entries, so one enumeration issues **59 × 5 = 295 sequential local HTTP request calls**, not 64 requests. It uses an isolated test router/fake registry, queue and spine plus service/store setup, not the production daemon. The inventory is **64 rows / 17,318 bytes**, parsed once for that test; classification uses BTreeSets and small fixed allowlists, with input/findings memory following the document size.

There is one standalone selected-library stage. A full harness/self-check that reaches both it and `rust-check`'s workspace tests runs the positive test **twice: 590 request calls, two JSON reads and two test-service/router setups**, plus Cargo/wrapper work. --quick skips the new heavy stage and Rust. Early self-check failures can prevent later work. HTTP enumeration has no explicit overall/client timeout. No new daemon runtime loop, listener or launch site ships: the production change is a cfg(test) module.

**Revised workshop:** the earlier cost block is addressed. It now requires in-process parent/start reads, refuses unreadable evidence without ProcLiveness/ps fallback, bounds the fresh walk to D=16, reaches the cache through the current peer prefix, charges hit/lifetime/boundary/incarnation checks, caps entries at 64 per incarnation plus a global cap, and retires lazily/on events rather than polling. Token hashing/map lookup is explicitly incremental authentication cost. Any argv probe stays in bounded bootstrap. Statusline/hook timers no longer undermine the no-launch recurring-path contract.

Before phase-2 code, fix the numeric global cache cap and efficient boundary/incarnation lookup budget; no per-hop whole-roster scans hidden under "binding lookup". Authorization correctness of cached suffixes/reparenting stays with security/reviewer; any validation they require must fit the stated bounded cost. These are design contracts, not implemented or measured authentication. The issuer-first/send-as-first order and q-02–q-04 separation are explicit; no messaging policy decision is implied by this cost review.
